messages:
rachel: anyone else seeing a spike of tiny GPU pods Pending in apse1-warm? ~90 pods. kubectl describe shows '0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu'. but prometheus/grafana shows GPUs idle on multiple nodes.

priya: that's odd. can you paste the describe and `kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,ALLOC:.status.allocatable,nvidia:.status.capacity` for one host?

rachel: describe snippet: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   3m    default-scheduler  0/6 nodes are available: 6 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```
and node alloc/cap for rack-r13-node-02: ALLOC: nvidia.com/gpu=0, CAPACITY: nvidia.com/gpu=4

tom: allocatable=0? that sounds like the device-plugin hasn't registered devices with the kubelet or kubelet set allocatables to 0 (device plugin unregister). any kubelet/device-plugin logs?

vlad: infra-bot shows device-plugin restarts after the firmware push last night to rack-r13 (nv-firmware-1.2.4) 

infra-bot: Node rack-r13-node-02: nvidia-device-plugin restarted 12 times since 2025-11-18T03:10:12Z. Kernel module reload triggered by firmware update.

priya: that would make the kubelet mark allocatable 0 while plugin is offline. prometheus GPU exporter still reports GPU usage from the host-level exporter even if kubelet allocatable is 0, so grafana can be misleading.

rachel: ok that maps. why did the plugin keep failing? logs show: `failed to list devices: NVML init error` then panic.

vlad: NVML errors usually mean driver mismatch with firmware or the driver wasn't reloaded before plugin start. The cluster reboot ordering started kubelets before the nvidia-driver daemonset re-applied nodes.

tom: quick mitigation plan: 1) cordon affected warm nodes so scheduler doesn't try to use them while we fix 2) patch device-plugin daemonset to add liveness/readiness backoff to avoid repeated unregisters 3) roll a node-level restart sequence to ensure driver is loaded before plugin.

priya: also we can temporarily add a scheduler predicate that allows pods to tolerate nodes with allocatable=0 but that seems risky. better: mark nodes Unschedulable until plugin healthy.

rachel: acceptance: we can't afford long cold-starts for inference-small. can we instead restart device-plugin gracefully and trigger kubelet to recompute allocatable without cordoning everything?

vlad: do `kubectl rollout restart ds nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system --field-selector spec.nodeName=rack-r13-node-02` won't work; daemonset restarts across nodes. we can delete the pod on specific node to force re-create after driver check.

priya: before deleting, let's check host driver state: `kubectl debug node/rack-r13-node-02 -it --image=busybox -- /bin/sh` then `nvidia-smi` inside. if nvidia-smi returns errors, need driver reinstall.

rachel: ran nvidia-smi via debug: returns valid output, shows 4 GPUs, but device-plugin logs still NVML init error right after starting. sequence shows kubelet starting device-plugin immediately after container runtime reports driver present, but plugin sometimes races with kernel module init.

tom: we should add a startup probe to device-plugin that waits for stable nvidia-smi for 10s before registering devices. I'll open a quick PR to add a retry loop with exponential backoff.

vlad: PR opened: infra/daemonsets#299 device-plugin: add startup probe and 5s jitter. will merge to canary first.

priya: in parallel, to relieve Pending pods, we can manually set `kubectl patch node rack-r13-node-02 -p '{"spec":{"unschedulable":true}}'` then delete the device-plugin pod to let it come up with backoff, then uncordon when healthy. Doing node-by-node to avoid mass eviction.

rachel: doing node-02 now. patch + delete plugin pod. waiting for new plugin to reach Ready.

infra-bot: Pod nvidia-device-plugin-r13-02 restarted at 2025-11-18T04:12:09Z. Startup probe failed 3 times, restart backoff in effect.

tom: hmm startup probe failing too. what does the plugin see? any permissions/selinux issue?

vlad: found root cause: after firmware update we also flipped a node-exporter feature flag that set `NVIDIA_REQUIRE_PERSISTENCE=0` on a subset of warm nodes. That env disables persistence daemon; plugin expects persistence to be enabled for stable NVML sessions. Combined with race on module init, plugin intermittently fails NVML init.

priya: rollback that env var for warm nodes and restart plugin pods on r13. That should restore allocatable quickly without cordoning the whole rack.

rachel: rolled env rollback on daemonset patch and restarted plugin on node-02. plugin came up healthy, kubelet reported allocatable nvidia.com/gpu=4 within 12s.

tom: great. now we should reschedule the Pending pods. scheduler will pick up new allocatable automatically. run descheduler nudge for the tiny inference pods: `kubectl create job deschedule-nudge --image=descheduler:stable -- <args>` to avoid piling everything onto one node.

rachel: after node-02 healthy, 26 pods scheduled. repeating for node-03/04.

priya: follow-up actions: 1) revert the feature-flag flip in node-exporter rollout (vlad) 2) add startup-backoff and NVML-wait to device-plugin (tom) 3) add alert for allocatable/capacity divergence in kube-state-metrics (priya) 4) postmortem doc to explain ordering and rollout steps (rachel).

vlad: logging the postmortem: INC-2025-4921. cost note: some warm nodes were underutilized but allocatable=0 kept scheduler from using them, causing extra burst capacity in Dedicated to pick up load -> potential extra spend for ~2h. finance pinged.

priya: for the alert: new rule: if sum(status.capacity[nvidia.com/gpu]) - sum(status.allocatable[nvidia.com/gpu]) >= 2 for >2m, fire pager. this catches device-plugin/kubelet mismatch.

rachel: final status: patched daemonset, restarted plugin across three nodes, pending tiny pods reduced to 0 after rolling fixes and descheduler nudge. no SLO breach. closing thread in 30m unless anyone has objections.

infra-bot: Incident updated: INC-2025-4921 resolved by device-plugin startup probe and node-exporter env rollback.

rachel: thanks all
